key_insight: A low-Reynolds-number propeller can exhibit thrust hysteresis during speed changes even when rotor-disk inflow, blade deformation, and sectional circulation remain largely quasi-steady.
engineering_relevance: Steady thrust maps may miss transient thrust deviations relevant to small-UAV control, despite low nondimensional acceleration levels.
method: Tested a two-bladed propeller in hover with pitch offsets of 0°, 5°, and 10°.
Applied open-loop acceleration and deceleration between 3000 and 5000 RPM.
Combined load measurements with phase-locked PIV at three radial stations and in the meridian plane.
evidence_signal: At the 5° pitch offset, thrust-coefficient deviations reached 8% during acceleration and 5% during deceleration; wake-related deviations were largest at low RPM rather than peak acceleration.
watch_item: The abstract inconsistently describes the 10° case as both quasi-steady and exhibiting deviations; verify pitch-dependent conclusions in the full paper.
paper_title: On the aerodynamics of an accelerating and decelerating propeller in hover at low Reynolds numbers
